lead.zh-Hans: 还没动身，我先把纸站错了边。
lead.en: Before setting off, I put my paper stops in the wrong order.

text.zh-Hans: 准备坐里约的缆车，我在便纸上写红海滩、乌尔卡山、糖面包山。纸拿反了，终点倒先到手边。旅人帮我转正，我又认真看了一遍。想把这一小段路画清楚寄回家，免得你读信也跟着我倒走。
text.en: Before riding Rio’s cable car, I wrote Praia Vermelha, Morro da Urca and Sugarloaf on a slip. Holding it upside down brought the destination to my thumb first. A traveler turned it around. I want a clear little drawing for home, so reading this letter will not mean traveling backward.
Talk through the paper stops
Connect the three stops

lead.zh-Hans: 兰花写在左边，铅笔滚去了右边。
lead.en: “Orchids” stayed left. The pencil rolled right.

text.zh-Hans: 里约植物园的收藏里有兰花和仙人掌。我想在便纸上各记一个名字，写完兰花，铅笔先滚到了桌边。我把它收回来，才继续写。今天寄给你的植物观察只有很短两行，照看铅笔的本事倒练长了一点。
text.en: Rio Botanical Garden’s collections include orchids and cacti. On my own note, I wrote one name before the pencil rolled toward the edge. Retrieved pencil, second name. The plant observation coming home is only two lines long. My pencil-minding skills have had a more substantial outing.
Tell the pencil’s little journey
Read the two lines carefully

lead.zh-Hans: 这顿午饭，让我把“走着说”改了。
lead.en: This lunch revised my plan to talk on the move.

text.zh-Hans: 吃里约的黑豆炖肉，我本来想边收包边想信的下一句。勺子还在手里，包带已经搭上肩。我索性把包放回去，坐稳吃饭。菜单上写黑豆与猪肉，信里写我终于肯好好坐着。两张纸都比赶路时清楚。
text.en: Over feijoada in Rio, I tried planning the next sentence while gathering my bag. Spoon in hand, strap on shoulder: neither task was going well. I put the bag down and ate seated. Black beans and pork went on the menu; my decision to sit still went in your letter.
Describe lunch after sitting down
Notice spoon and bag in place

lead.zh-Hans: 脆饼的声音，比我写字快。
lead.en: The biscuit finished its sound before I finished the word.

text.zh-Hans: 在里约尝木薯脆饼，咬下一口就有脆响。我写“咔嚓”，还没落完最后一笔，下一口已经吃好了。于是先收笔，免得给自己寄一封全是响声的信。菜单边上留下几笔短线，我想你看见就能猜到一点。
text.en: A tapioca biscuit in Rio gave a quick crackle. Writing the sound took longer than eating the next bite. I put down the pencil before my entire letter became noise. A few short strokes remain beside the menu drawing. I think they will give you the idea.
Read the sound on paper
Find where the short strokes end

lead.zh-Hans: 把午饭讲完，需要给勺子放个假。
lead.en: Telling lunch’s story required a break for the spoon.

text.zh-Hans: 我把里约的炖肉和脆饼说给旅人听，刚开口就发现手里还握着勺子，只好先放下。两张菜单摆好，我指着它们讲自己怎么吃得太忙。对方说，纸上的午饭倒很从容。我把这句记下来，好在给你的信里也慢一点。
text.en: Telling a traveler about Rio feijoada and tapioca biscuits, I noticed I still held my spoon. I set it down and laid out the menus. “Your paper lunch looks unhurried,” they said, after hearing about my busy hands. I kept the remark as a reminder to slow down in this letter too.
Finish the meal’s story slowly
Notice the space left by the spoon

lead.zh-Hans: 一点深色，几笔短线，都各归各页。
lead.en: Dark dots and short strokes found separate pages.

text.zh-Hans: 里约菜单上的黑豆，我用深色小点记，脆饼则用短线记。收纸时不小心叠在一起，透过去像一盘很忙的饭。我分开检查，写好菜名，再夹回自己的纸套。今天的细看，有一半是在照看自己的粗心。
text.en: Dark dots stood for black beans on my Rio menu; short strokes for crisp biscuits. Accidentally overlaid, the sheets looked like one very busy plate. I separated them, checked the names and returned them to their sleeves. Half of today’s close observation has been directed at my own muddles.
Talk about that overlaid lunch
Study dots and strokes separately

lead.zh-Hans: 照你说的“{reply}”，线终于往前走了。
lead.en: With “{reply},” the line finally went forward.

text.zh-Hans: 我把红海滩、乌尔卡山和糖面包山的名字重新写好，按你的回应接成一条线，再折成小小的三页纸。它记的是我在里约这一段路，不是正式路线图。翻开一页，下一站就露出来，终点这回没有抢着出发。
text.en: Following your reply, I joined Praia Vermelha, Morro da Urca and Sugarloaf on a line, then folded the sheet into three small panels. It records my own Rio journey, not an official route map. Turning a panel reveals the next stop. This time the destination waits its turn.
Tell the journey panel by panel
Open the next little panel

lead.zh-Hans: 围巾一拉，邮包也跟着往上走。
lead.en: I pulled my scarf, and the mailbag came up with it.

text.zh-Hans: 到了乌尔卡山，我把围巾往外一拉，邮包也跟着升了起来。重来里约，糖面包山缆车接下来的方向我还认得，偏偏自己打的结解不开。旁边的旅人替我托着包，我才摸出围巾的一头，原来它从提手里穿了过去。我红着脸把围巾慢慢抽出来，重新搭好围巾。对方松手时，我胸前终于只剩一个软软的结。
text.en: At Morro da Urca, I tugged my scarf and lifted my mailbag with it. Back in Rio, I could remember where the cable car continued towards Sugarloaf Mountain, yet I could not work out what I had tied around myself. Another traveller held the bag while I followed one end of the scarf. It had gone straight through the handle. I eased it free, feeling rather warm around the ears. When my helper let go, only a soft scarf knot rested against my chest.

text.zh-Hans: 谢谢替我托住包的旅人
text.en: Thank the traveller who held the bag

text.zh-Hans: 找找围巾从哪里穿过去了
text.en: Trace where the scarf went through the handle
